key_insight: The Nephro Candidate Score (N-CS) combines gene, variant, and inheritance signals to prioritize likely disease-causing variants in suspected inherited kidney disease.
clinical_relevance: This tool may help clinicians and researchers focus genetic testing on the most plausible candidate variants and genes, potentially improving diagnosis and discovery in kidney disease.
method: Built a machine learning pipeline with a Nephro Gene Score (N-GS) for gene-disease relevance and a Nephro Variant Score (N-VS) for pathogenicity.
Added a heuristic inheritance score to integrate family-pattern information.
Validated performance on independent test sets and in a cohort of 1,452 individuals with suspected inherited kidney disease.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the N-GS reached an AUC of 0.94 and the N-VS reached an AUC of 0.99, with enrichment of kidney-related biology and external support for 10 of 11 newly proposed genes.
watch_item: Performance may not fully translate across diverse clinical settings, and prioritized candidates still require expert review and confirmatory genetic/clinical evidence.
paper_title: Automated Variant Prioritization in Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease
